html:
Apollonia was an ancient city near today's Fier in Albania, founded around 588 BCE by Greek colonists from Corinth and Corfu, one of many cities of the Greek colonisation of the Adriatic.

It grew rich on trade with the Illyrian interior and later stood at the western end of the Via Egnatia. Under Rome it was a free city and a centre of learning: the young Octavian, the future Augustus, was studying there in 44 BCE when he heard of Caesar's murder. Cicero praised it as a great and important city. In the 200s CE an earthquake shifted the course of the river, the harbour silted up and the city declined. A Byzantine monastery stands among its ruins.
sum: Apollonia was an ancient city near today's Fier in Albania, founded around 588 BCE by Greek colonists from Corinth and Corfu, one of many cities of the Greek colonisation of the Adriatic.
